zh.lead: 示例章的每一页对应语料的一个分组。每条示例给两个 tab：默认显示「画面」——它在真 Chromium 里渲染出的终态截图（`scripts/shot-corpus.mjs` 逐条落图）；切到「代码」看该条语料的完整源码（直接引自 `corpus/examples/`，不复制一份）。
zh.note: `net`（需联网取包）与 `reject`（预期被当场拒绝）两组没有截图，不进示例章：前者是取包链路的回归，见[第三方包](/guide/packages)；后者是拦截口径的回归，见[支持面](/guide/support)。最后一组[引擎扩展](/examples/extras)是**另一条车道**：那些图形标准 Manim 没有，代码里要 `from manim_live_extra import …`，本机 CLI 导出会被前置门拒绝——它单独成页，别与前 17 页混用。

en.lead: Each page of this chapter corresponds to one corpus group. Every example offers two tabs: the default is Rendered — its end-state screenshot taken entry by entry in a real Chromium by `scripts/shot-corpus.mjs`; switching to Code shows the example's full source (imported straight from `corpus/examples/`, not copied).
en.note: The `net` group (packages fetched over the network) and the `reject` group (expected to be refused on the spot) have no screenshots and are not part of this chapter: the former regresses the fetch path, see [Third-Party Packages](/en/guide/packages); the latter regresses the refusal vocabulary, see [Support Surface](/en/guide/support). The last group, [Engine extensions](/en/examples/extras), is a **separate lane**: those shapes do not exist in standard Manim, the code must say `from manim_live_extra import …`, and a local CLI export is refused by the export gate — it has a page of its own, so do not mix it with the 17 pages above.

intro.zh: 圆、矩形、椭圆、弧、多边形、星形这些基本形，以及线、点、箭头的各种变体。
intro.en: The basic shapes — circle, rectangle, ellipse, arc, polygons, star — plus the line, dot and arrow variants.

intro.zh: 位置参数与关键字参数怎么收：半径、边长、坐标、向量、控制点，以及 VGroup 的变长参数。
intro.en: How positional and keyword arguments are taken: radius, side length, coordinates, vectors, control points, and VGroup's variadic arguments.

intro.zh: set_stroke / set_fill 这类改写、shift / rotate 这类变换链、save_state / restore 与 copy 的边界。
intro.en: Style rewrites such as set_stroke / set_fill, transform chains like shift / rotate, and the boundaries of save_state / restore and copy.

intro.zh: 数轴、网格、坐标轴标签、c2p 坐标换算、曲线面积与黎曼矩形，以及柱状图、矩阵与表格。
intro.en: Number lines, grids, axis labels, c2p coordinate mapping, area and Riemann rectangles, plus bar charts, matrices and tables.

intro.zh: Text / MathTex / Tex / MarkupText 的渲染与排版，列表、折行、下划线、数字动画与标题。
intro.en: Rendering and typesetting of Text / MathTex / Tex / MarkupText, plus lists, wrapping, underlines, number animations and titles.

intro.zh: 推导式、解包、闭包、生成器、dataclass、装饰器、异常与上下文管理器——只用 manim 加标准库，离线可跑。
intro.en: Comprehensions, unpacking, closures, generators, dataclasses, decorators, exceptions and context managers — manim plus the standard library only, runnable offline.

intro.zh: m.animate 链、速率函数、Transform 一族、入场与高亮动画、沿路径运动与描边后填充。
intro.en: m.animate chains, rate functions, the Transform family, entrance and highlight animations, motion along a path, and draw-border-then-fill.

intro.zh: TracedPath 轨迹、tracker 驱动、(m, dt) 更新器、clear_updaters 与 UpdateFromFunc 一族。
intro.en: TracedPath trails, tracker-driven positions, (m, dt) updaters, clear_updaters and the UpdateFromFunc family.

intro.zh: clear / remove 的场景语义、VGroup 的下标与嵌套、循环搭建，以及 3D 相机的「正」。
intro.en: Scene semantics of clear / remove, VGroup indexing and nesting, loop-built groups, and what an upright 3D camera looks like.

intro.zh: 数列极限、夹逼、泰勒、e 的定义、中值定理、上下和、变上限积分、偏导、梯度下降、二重积分、傅里叶与级数。
intro.en: Sequence limits, the squeeze theorem, Taylor expansion, the definition of e, the mean value theorem, upper and lower sums, accumulation functions, partial derivatives, gradient descent, double integrals, Fourier series and partial sums.

intro.zh: 矩阵乘向量、行列式面积、奇异矩阵、投影、Gram–Schmidt、特征分解、秩与零空间、基变换、最小二乘、二次型与 SVD。
intro.en: Matrix-vector products, determinant as area, singular matrices, projection, Gram–Schmidt, eigen decomposition, rank and null space, basis change, least squares, quadratic forms and SVD.

intro.zh: 容斥、条件概率、贝叶斯树、期望与方差、大数定律、中心极限、泊松、3σ 法则、蒙特卡洛 π、随机游走与假设检验。
intro.en: Inclusion–exclusion, conditional probability, Bayes trees, expectation and variance, the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, Poisson arrivals, the 3σ rule, Monte Carlo π, random walks and hypothesis tests.

intro.zh: 循环群、Cayley 表、二面体群、生成元与子群、拉格朗日、置换复合、同态核、商群、子群格与轨道-稳定子。
intro.en: Cyclic groups, Cayley tables, dihedral groups, generators and subgroups, Lagrange's theorem, permutation composition, homomorphism kernels, quotient groups, subgroup lattices and orbit-stabilizer.

intro.zh: 真值表、幂集格、关系矩阵、等价类、哈斯图、归纳法、鸽巢、二分图、着色、最小生成树、欧拉与哈密顿回路、汉诺塔递推。
intro.en: Truth tables, power-set lattices, relation matrices, equivalence classes, Hasse diagrams, induction, pigeonhole, bipartite graphs, colouring, minimum spanning trees, Euler and Hamilton cycles, and the Hanoi recurrence.

intro.zh: 通用讲解范式：单位圆、正弦波追踪、勾股、极坐标、割线趋近、黎曼和、线性变换与概率对照。
intro.en: Reusable lesson patterns: unit circle, sine-wave tracing, Pythagoras, polar curves, secant-to-tangent, Riemann sums, linear maps and probability comparisons.

intro.zh: 把支持面表里 state=ok 的名字成批点名：76 个颜色、16 个速率、方向常量、方法面、形状与 3D 实体、动画面与复平面。
intro.en: Batch-naming every entry marked ok in the support table: 76 colours, 16 rate functions, direction constants, the method surface, shapes and 3D solids, the animation surface, and the complex plane.

intro.zh: pandas / scipy / sklearn / statsmodels / matplotlib 与 Manim 串成一条讲解管线，需联网取包。
intro.en: pandas / scipy / sklearn / statsmodels / matplotlib chained into one Manim lesson pipeline; fetching the packages needs network access.

intro.zh: **这些不是原版 Manim 的图形。** 它们在引擎扩展车道上：代码里要写 `from manim_live_extra import …`，只在本套引擎里渲染；本机 CLI 导出会被导出前置门当场拒绝（见[支持面](/guide/support)）。本页 34 个图形按用途分：统计与通用图表 14、数学可视化 2、生物 3、化学 1、机器学习 5、概率 1、网络与流程 1、3D 5、分形 2。
intro.en: **These are not standard Manim mobjects.** They live on the engine-extension lane: the code must say `from manim_live_extra import …`, they render only in this engine, and a local CLI export is refused up front by the export gate (see [Support Surface](/en/guide/support)). The 34 shapes on this page group by purpose: charts and statistics 14, maths visualisation 2, biology 3, chemistry 1, machine learning 5, probability 1, network and flow 1, 3D 5, fractals 2.

extras-histogram.title: Histogram
extras-histogram.expect: A four-bar histogram whose bar heights are the bucket counts (rising to the right), with axes drawn automatically.

extras-boxplot.title: Box plot (BoxPlot)
extras-boxplot.expect: Two box plots side by side (box, whiskers, outliers); the left group sits overall higher than the right.

extras-violinplot.title: Violin plot (ViolinPlot)
extras-violinplot.expect: Two violins (kernel-density outlines) side by side, each swelling where the data is densest.

extras-scatterplot.title: Scatter plot (ScatterPlot)
extras-scatterplot.expect: A cloud of positively correlated points (larger x, larger y) with axes drawn automatically.

extras-stacked-bar.title: Stacked bar chart (StackedBarChart)
extras-stacked-bar.expect: Three bars, each stacked from two colour segments (blue below, green above), with a legend.

extras-area-chart.title: Area chart (AreaChart)
extras-area-chart.expect: Two bands filled down to the baseline in different colours, partially overlapping and rippling with x.

extras-step-chart.title: Step chart (StepChart)
extras-step-chart.expect: A staircase polyline that jumps horizontally then vertically between data points, each point marked with a dot.

extras-calendar-heatmap.title: Calendar heatmap (CalendarHeatmap)
extras-calendar-heatmap.expect: A row of week-aligned cells (a calendar) whose shading follows each day’s value.

extras-pie-chart.title: Pie chart (PieChart)
extras-pie-chart.expect: A pie in three slices (2:1:1) with a text label on each.

extras-donut-chart.title: Donut chart (DonutChart)
extras-donut-chart.expect: A hollow three-colour ring (3:2:1) with the canvas showing through the middle.

extras-radar-chart.title: Radar chart (RadarChart)
extras-radar-chart.expect: A pentagonal grid with a data polygon laid over it (five uneven dimensions), each axis labelled.

extras-gantt-chart.title: Gantt chart (GanttChart)
extras-gantt-chart.expect: Two timeline bars (research first, development after and overlapping) with time on the horizontal axis and task names per row.

extras-heatmap.title: Scalar-field heat map (HeatMap)
extras-heatmap.expect: A field of cells coloured by a function’s value, bright at the centre and fading outward, in a continuous colour ramp with no grid lines.

extras-contour-plot.title: Contour plot (ContourPlot)
extras-contour-plot.expect: Nested closed contour lines (a few rings on a saddle surface); where the lines crowd, the gradient is steep.

extras-candlestick.title: Candlestick chart (CandlestickChart)
extras-candlestick.expect: Three candlesticks with bodies and both wicks; gains are red and losses green (the Chinese convention, passed explicitly).

extras-waterfall.title: Waterfall chart (WaterfallChart)
extras-waterfall.expect: Four rise-and-fall segments plus a total bar, joined by connector lines, walking from 3 up to 6.

extras-dna-helix.title: DNA double helix (DNAHelix)
extras-dna-helix.expect: Two backbone strands winding in opposite directions with base-pair rungs between them, coloured by base.

extras-cell.title: Cell diagram (Cell)
extras-cell.expect: A round membrane, a nucleus, and several organelles, each labelled.

extras-amino-acid.title: Amino-acid chain (AminoAcidChain)
extras-amino-acid.expect: A string of beads coloured by residue with peptide-bond links between them.

extras-molecule.title: Molecular structure (MoleculeMobject)
extras-molecule.expect: A water molecule in skeletal form: the oxygen labelled O, two hydrogens labelled H, bonds drawn as lines.

extras-neural-network.title: Neural network (NeuralNetwork)
extras-neural-network.expect: Three layers of nodes spread left to right with every adjacent pair fully connected, centred in the frame.

extras-feed-forward-layer.title: Fully connected layer (FeedForwardLayer)
extras-feed-forward-layer.expect: A column of four evenly spaced dots.

extras-conv-layer.title: Convolutional layer (ConvolutionalLayer)
extras-conv-layer.expect: Three 3×3 feature-map squares side by side.

extras-pooling-layer.title: Pooling layer (PoolingLayer)
extras-pooling-layer.expect: Three 2×2 feature-map squares side by side.

extras-image-layer.title: Image layer (ImageLayer)
extras-image-layer.expect: A single 5×5 grid of pixel cells.

extras-dice-face.title: Dice face (DiceFace)
extras-dice-face.expect: A rounded square carrying five pips laid out as the 5 face.

extras-sankey.title: Sankey diagram (SankeyDiagram)
extras-sankey.expect: Two nodes on the left feeding two on the right, with flow ribbons whose width matches the flow.

extras-box3d.title: Cuboid (Box3D)
extras-box3d.expect: A cuboid standing on an axis, its faces shaded, unmistakably 3D at a slanted angle.

extras-vector3d.title: 3D vector (Vector3D)
extras-vector3d.expect: An arrowed vector reaching out from the origin among three axes.

extras-parametric-surface.title: Parametric surface (ParametricSurface)
extras-parametric-surface.expect: A saddle-shaped surface swept out by u and v, with three axes.

extras-surface3d.title: Surface (Surface3D)
extras-surface3d.expect: An upward-curving paraboloid with three axes.

extras-implicit-surface.title: Implicit surface (ImplicitSurface)
extras-implicit-surface.expect: A sphere cut out as the level set x²+y²+z²=1.

extras-mandelbrot.title: Mandelbrot set (MandelbrotSet)
extras-mandelbrot.expect: A full fractal picture: the cardioid body with small discs around it and colour bands at the boundary.

extras-newton-fractal.title: Newton fractal (NewtonFractal)
extras-newton-fractal.expect: A three-colour fractal partitioned by the cube roots of unity, with fine texture along the boundaries.

basic-circle.title: Draw a circle
basic-circle.expect: A circle in the default stroke colour appears at the centre of the frame, drawn by Create tracing its outline.

basic-square-rotate.title: Rotate a square by 45°
basic-square-rotate.expect: The square rotates 45° about its own centre; position and size stay put.

basic-rect-rounded.title: Rectangle and rounded rectangle
basic-rect-rounded.expect: A plain rectangle beside a rounded one; the smoothed corners are a visible difference.

basic-ellipse-annulus.title: Ellipse and annulus
basic-ellipse-annulus.expect: An ellipse and an annulus; the ring is hollow (an inner and an outer radius).

basic-arc-sector.title: Arc and sector
basic-arc-sector.expect: An arc (stroke only) and a sector (arc plus two radii plus fill).

basic-polygons.title: Triangle and regular hexagon
basic-polygons.expect: A triangle and a regular hexagon side by side; the edge counts match the names.

basic-star.title: Six-pointed star
basic-star.expect: A six-pointed star outline with six crisp tips.

basic-polygon-vertices.title: Polygon from vertices
basic-polygon-vertices.expect: A polygon connecting the given vertices in order; the shape matches the coordinates.

basic-axes-plot.title: Axes plus a function curve
basic-axes-plot.expect: A function curve on a set of axes; the curve follows the function and sits on the ticks.

basic-line-dot-arrow.title: Line, dot, arrow
basic-line-dot-arrow.expect: One line, one dot and one arrow: the arrow carries a tip on one end and the dot sits where specified.

basic-line-variants.title: Dashed, double arrow, arc arrow
basic-line-variants.expect: The dashed line is broken, the double arrow has tips on both ends and the arc arrow curves — all three distinguishable at a glance.

ctor-circle-positional.title: Circle positional argument (radius)
ctor-circle-positional.expect: Two circles given only a radius differ in size; the radius values match the picture.

ctor-square-positional.title: Square positional argument (side length)
ctor-square-positional.expect: Two squares given only a side length differ in size.

ctor-dot-positional.title: Dot positional argument (coordinates)
ctor-dot-positional.expect: The dot lands at the given coordinates, not at the default origin.

ctor-text-kwargs.title: Text weight, style and size
ctor-text-kwargs.expect: Several Text runs differ visibly in weight, italics and font size.

ctor-vector.title: Vector positional argument
ctor-vector.expect: One arrow whose direction and length match the vector passed in.

ctor-parametric.title: ParametricFunction positional argument
ctor-parametric.expect: A curve drawn from the parametric equations; the shape matches them (neither a circle nor a line).

ctor-function-graph.title: FunctionGraph takes a function
ctor-function-graph.expect: The curve's shape matches the function passed in.

ctor-right-angle.title: RightAngle takes two lines
ctor-right-angle.expect: A right-angle mark (a small elbow) stands at the intersection of the two lines.

ctor-angle-points.title: Angle takes three points
ctor-angle-points.expect: The arc opens across the angle determined by the three points; its opening matches the angle.

ctor-brace.title: Brace takes one mobject
ctor-brace.expect: A brace hugs one side of the mobject, its length matching the mobject.

ctor-brace-between.title: BraceBetweenPoints takes two points
ctor-brace-between.expect: A brace spans the two points, aligned with their connecting line and scaled to their distance.

ctor-cubic-bezier.title: CubicBezier takes four points
ctor-cubic-bezier.expect: The curve follows a cubic Bézier through the four control points, with its endpoints on the first and fourth.

ctor-value-tracker.title: ValueTracker takes an initial value
ctor-value-tracker.expect: ValueTracker draws nothing (it is only a number); the scene renders without error and the other mobjects behave.

ctor-vgroup-variadic.title: VGroup variadic positional arguments
ctor-vgroup-variadic.expect: Several mobjects gathered into one VGroup move as a whole; their relative positions stay fixed.

method-set-stroke.title: set_stroke (mapped to setStyle)
method-set-stroke.expect: Only the stroke changes (width / colour) while the fill stays as it was — set_stroke wiping the fill was a fixed incident and this case pins it.

method-set-opacity.title: set_opacity (split into stroke + fill)
method-set-opacity.expect: Stroke and fill fade together; the colour is unchanged.

method-set-fill.title: set_fill keyword opacity
method-set-fill.expect: The fill becomes the given colour with the given opacity; the stroke is untouched.

method-put-start-and-end-on.title: put_start_and_end_on (Line in two steps)
method-put-start-and-end-on.expect: The line's two ends land exactly on the two given points.

method-next-to-buff.title: next_to with buff
method-next-to-buff.expect: The gap between the two mobjects matches the buff value — neither touching nor too far apart.

method-edge-corner.title: to_edge / to_corner
method-edge-corner.expect: The mobject sticks to the given edge or corner, keeping a buff from the border.

method-process-family.title: shift / move_to / scale / rotate chain
method-process-family.expect: The four calls chain in order; the final position and orientation match the chain.

method-arrange-grid.title: arrange_in_grid
method-arrange-grid.expect: A set of mobjects laid out in a tidy grid with the requested rows, columns and spacing.

method-save-restore.title: save_state / restore
method-save-restore.expect: After the changes, restore returns the mobject to its save_state look — position, size and style all back.

method-become.title: become swaps the shape
method-become.expect: After playback the mobject has become the target shape; become replaces rather than copies.

method-attr-read.title: Reading the width attribute
method-attr-read.expect: The printed width matches the mobject's real width (the numeric assertion is authoritative).

method-get-center.title: get_center used for placement
method-get-center.expect: A mobject placed with get_center's return value has its centre exactly where expected.

method-copy.title: copy produces a new mobject
method-copy.expect: Changing the copy leaves the original untouched — the two are independent and share no style.

graph-number-line.title: Number line with numbers
graph-number-line.expect: One number line; ticks and tick numbers agree and the spacing is even.

graph-number-plane.title: Plane grid
graph-number-plane.expect: A plane grid with both directions of lines complete and evenly spaced.

graph-axes-labels.title: Axes with axis labels
graph-axes-labels.expect: Axes with arrow tips and x / y labels; the labels sit at the axis ends.

graph-graph-label.title: Label on a curve
graph-graph-label.expect: A label hugs its curve without leaving the frame or covering the line.

graph-c2p.title: c2p maps coordinates to canvas positions
graph-c2p.expect: The marker lands exactly at the position c2p computes; the printed numbers match the picture.

graph-area.title: Area under a curve
graph-area.expect: A translucent fill between the curve and the x axis, bounded by the curve segment.

graph-riemann.title: Riemann rectangles
graph-riemann.expect: A row of rectangles along the underside of the curve, heights following the sampled function values.

graph-bar-chart.title: Bar chart
graph-bar-chart.expect: Three bars in red / blue / green with heights matching the data and even spacing; the title sits above without covering the chart.

graph-matrix.title: Matrix
graph-matrix.expect: A matrix laid out by rows and columns; the entries match the input.

graph-table.title: Table with a header
graph-table.expect: A table with a header row; rows and columns aligned and all grid lines present.

graph-integer-table.title: IntegerTable (numbers written directly)
graph-integer-table.expect: Integers fill the cells directly (no LaTeX number formatting); the contents match.

graph-math-table.title: LaTeX table
graph-math-table.expect: The table content is typeset as LaTeX (math fonts), not plain text fonts.

text-basic.title: Text
text-basic.expect: Text renders with real glyphs (no boxes or mojibake); the content matches.

text-mathtex-frac.title: MathTex fraction and root
text-mathtex-frac.expect: The fraction has its bar and the root covers its radicand, in math typesetting.

text-tex-plain.title: Tex takes a LaTeX string
text-tex-plain.expect: A whole LaTeX string typeset as a formula with normal fonts and spacing.

text-markup.title: MarkupText rich text
text-markup.expect: Local bold / colour changes in the rich text take effect; the rest is unaffected.

text-bulleted-list.title: BulletedList
text-bulleted-list.expect: Each list line carries a bullet and the line spacing is even.

text-paragraph.title: Paragraph auto-wraps
text-paragraph.expect: A long string wraps into several lines without exceeding the line width.

text-underline.title: Underline
text-underline.expect: A line under the text, its length matching the text.

text-decimal-number.title: DecimalNumber animation
text-decimal-number.expect: A number animation: digit and decimal counts follow the parameters and the value changes continuously during playback.

text-mathtex-corner.title: Two-digit label at the top-right corner
text-mathtex-corner.expect: A two-digit label sits at the target's top-right corner, inside the frame and off the target (a fixed positioning incident).

text-mathtex-parts.title: MathTex multiple positional parts
text-mathtex-parts.expect: Several parts laid out on one line with sensible spacing and the given order.

text-title.title: Title
text-title.expect: The title appears centred at the top of the frame, larger than body text.

updater-traced-path.title: TracedPath follows a mobject
updater-traced-path.expect: A trail line grows behind the moving dot and coincides with the path travelled.

updater-value-driven.title: Position driven by a tracker
updater-value-driven.expect: As the tracker's value is animated, the dot moves to the matching position (printed coordinates agree with the picture). Self-evidence: tick 2 on the NumberLine at the bottom coincides with where the red dot settles.

updater-with-dt.title: Updater taking (m, dt)
updater-with-dt.expect: A (m, dt) updater advances with real time during wait, not only during animations.

updater-clear.title: clear_updaters stops the following
updater-clear.expect: After clear_updaters the mobject stays put: further tracker changes no longer move it.

updater-decimal.title: Number follows the tracker
updater-decimal.expect: The number follows the tracker live; it does not jump to the final value at the end.

updater-update-from-func.title: Animations driving update functions (UpdateFromFunc / UpdateFromAlphaFunc)
updater-update-from-func.expect: The update function is driven during the animation and the m it receives answers to CE method names (a fixed wrapping incident).

animate-chain.title: m.animate chain
animate-chain.expect: The square moves right, then changes colour, then scales (several changes on one chain land together); the motion is smooth.

animate-chain-fill.title: Changing the fill inside an animate chain
animate-chain-fill.expect: At the end the fill is the target colour, reached by a gradient rather than an instant jump.

animate-rate-func.title: Rate and duration (rate_func comparison)
animate-rate-func.expect: Two mobjects travel the same distance left to right in the same run_time, one with rate_func=linear and one with rate_func=smooth, each labelled with its rate name; the frame keeps the start and end marks of both paths. The pacing difference (smooth is slow at both ends, fast in the middle) is processual — observe it in real time; the final frame testifies through the path + endpoint marks + rate-name labels.

animate-rate-variants.title: there_and_back rate
animate-rate-variants.expect: The mobject reaches the target and returns along the same path to the start (the signature behaviour of there_and_back). The return is processual — observe it in real time; in the final frame the circle is back at the start while the target dot and the dashed path stay as evidence, with there_and_back labelled beside the circle.

animate-transform.title: Transform
animate-transform.expect: Mobject A morphs continuously into mobject B (shape and position interpolated together); throughout, both are the same mobject.

animate-replacement-transform.title: ReplacementTransform replaces the old mobject
animate-replacement-transform.expect: After the morph the scene holds B and A is gone — moving A afterwards never brings it back.

animate-transform-matching-tex.title: TransformMatchingTex formula morph
animate-transform-matching-tex.expect: Identical fragments of the formula stay in place while different fragments move into position, instead of shuffling the whole string (yellow = unchanged from a = b to x = y, with a→x and b→y filling the gaps).

animate-lagged-start.title: LaggedStart staggered entrance
animate-lagged-start.expect: Several mobjects enter one after another with a stagger; lag_ratio sets how much they overlap.

animate-animation-group.title: AnimationGroup in parallel
animate-animation-group.expect: The animations in the group run at the same time and finish together, not one by one.

animate-indicate-family.title: Indicate / Flash / Circumscribe
animate-indicate-family.expect: Indicate is a scale flash in place, Flash is a burst of light at a point, Circumscribe draws a ring around the mobject — three distinct shapes. All three highlights are processual — observe them in real time; the final frame distinguishes them by name labels and keeps a ring for Circumscribe (a hand-computed Rectangle added explicitly after the animation) as evidence.

animate-move-along-path.title: MoveAlongPath follows a path
animate-move-along-path.expect: The dot travels along the given path curve, not along a straight line.

animate-rotating.title: Rotating about an axis
animate-rotating.expect: The mobject turns continuously about the given axis (several turns or a given angle), not snapping into place.

animate-scale-in-place.title: ScaleInPlace
animate-scale-in-place.expect: The mobject scales up or down in place; its centre does not move.

animate-draw-border.title: DrawBorderThenFill
animate-draw-border.expect: The outline is drawn first and only then does the fill arrive — two visible phases. Border-first, fill-later is processual — observe it in real time; the adapter does not settle the fill at the animation's end state, so a set_fill animation is appended afterwards and the final frame shows a fully yellow-filled square.

animate-apply-matrix.title: ApplyMatrix
animate-apply-matrix.expect: The mobject is skewed or rotated by the matrix — a shear or rotation deformation, not a translation or uniform scale.

animate-fade-family.title: FadeIn / FadeOut
animate-fade-family.expect: FadeIn fades in from transparent and FadeOut fades out to nothing; everything else is unchanged. Fading is processual — observe it in real time; readable evidence in the final frame: the top title stays throughout as a reference, the FadeIn triangle remains visible, and the FadeOut circle is gone.

animate-grow-family.title: GrowFromEdge / GrowFromCenter
animate-grow-family.expect: GrowFromCenter grows out of the centre while GrowFromEdge grows along the given edge — different directions.

scene-clear.title: Redraw after clear
scene-clear.expect: clear empties the frame; the mobjects drawn afterwards appear on their own.

scene-remove.title: remove takes a mobject out
scene-remove.expect: The removed mobject disappears while the others stay as they were: the scene holds three mobjects and only one is removed (the red circle, labelled remove); in the final frame the blue square and the yellow triangle remain and the red circle does not — evidence that exactly one was removed.

scene-vgroup-index.title: VGroup plus index access
scene-vgroup-index.expect: An indexed child is manipulated on its own; an out-of-range index raises IndexError (the print assertion is authoritative).

scene-vgroup-nested.title: VGroup inside VGroup
scene-vgroup-nested.expect: The outer group moves as a whole and the inner group moves on its own; the two layers do not leak into each other. Self-evidence: after the outer group moves up the red dot follows, then the inner group turns yellow on its own while the red dot's colour stays.

scene-loop-build.title: Building a row of squares in a loop
scene-loop-build.expect: A row (column) of squares built in a loop; the count matches the iteration count.

scene-three-d-upright.title: The upright 3D camera: the x axis must be horizontal on screen
scene-three-d-upright.expect: Five cubes form a true cross: red (x=-4) on the left and blue (x=+4) on the right at exactly the same height; yellow (y=+3) above and orange (y=-3) below at exactly the same horizontal position as the green centre cube. Each cube shows its top and front face (lit, with depth).

lesson-unit-circle.title: Unit circle and trigonometric lines
lesson-unit-circle.expect: A point travels on the unit circle while the sine / cosine lines stretch with the angle; their lengths match the angle.

lesson-sine-wave-trace.title: Tracing a sine wave from a point on the circle
lesson-sine-wave-trace.expect: As the point on the circle turns, the wave unfolds to the right and what is drawn is exactly the sine curve (a full sine of amplitude ±1.2, observed in real time; with turbo screenshots the sparse frames can collapse a TracedPath trail into a straight line — a screenshot artefact).

lesson-pythagorean.title: The Pythagorean theorem
lesson-pythagorean.expect: Squares on the three sides of a right triangle present the area relation a² + b² = c².

lesson-polar-rose.title: Polar rose curve
lesson-polar-rose.expect: The petal count matches the equation parameters: left k=5 gives 5 petals (k odd), right k=2 gives 4 petals (2k petals, k even); each curve carries its equation label so the odd-k → k petals / even-k → 2k petals rule is readable by comparison.

lesson-polar-spiral.title: Archimedean spiral
lesson-polar-spiral.expect: The spiral widens turn by turn with a constant gap between turns (the defining trait of an Archimedean spiral).

lesson-secant-tangent.title: Secants approaching the tangent (the definition of the derivative)
lesson-secant-tangent.expect: The secant rotates about the tangency point, hugging the tangent ever closer until they coincide.

lesson-riemann-sum.title: Riemann sums approaching the integral
lesson-riemann-sum.expect: The rectangles get finer and their area sum approaches the definite integral: the coarse dx=1 rectangles stay in the final frame as stroked ghosts next to the fine dx=0.25 ones, and the two labels on the right give both area sums (1.60 → 2.63, true value 2.27).

lesson-linear-rotate.title: Linear map: rotation
lesson-linear-rotate.expect: Grid and vectors rotate 30° as a whole (not a multiple of 90°, so the tilted orientation is obvious) without changing shape; the matrix is written in cos/sin 30° form, the green arrow is 2 cells long and still aligns with the grid ticks after rotation.

lesson-linear-shear.title: Linear map: shear
lesson-linear-shear.expect: The grid is sheared: rows shift horizontally and columns tilt; the pre-image grid stays in place as a low-opacity ghost for comparison, and a 1×1 reference square becomes a parallelogram with the same base and height — area per cell unchanged (det=1), visibly.

lesson-eigenvector.title: Linear map: eigen directions
lesson-eigenvector.expect: Vectors on an eigen direction stay on that direction after the map (red v₁ stretched 3× along the dashed line, blue v₂ unmoved) while the grey control vector u leaves its direction — deflected and undeflected side by side; the dashed lines are the two eigen directions. The three pre-image vectors stay in place as translucent ghosts, with λ₁=3 / λ₂=1 labels near the arrow tips.

lesson-probability-dice.title: Probability: frequency of dice rolls
lesson-probability-dice.expect: The more rolls, the flatter the six frequency bars become (approaching uniform): six nearly equal bars (15%–18%), each measured value hovering around the orange dashed line at the theoretical 16.7%.

lesson-probability-binomial.title: Probability: binomial distribution
lesson-probability-binomial.expect: Two binomial pmf polylines side by side: n=10 peaks near 0.25 and n=30 near 0.14 — same p, larger n gives a shorter and wider distribution; the two-way comparison carries the claim that the parameters decide the shape.

lesson-space-cube-camera.title: Spatial Cartesian coordinates and a cube
lesson-space-cube-camera.expect: A cube of edge 2 seen at an angle: three faces visible at once with different shading (lit and with depth, not a black blob); it sits in the first octant with a yellow dot and label on its farthest vertex (2, 2, 2); the three axes leave the origin with Z pointing up. The title is pinned to the top-left of the frame and does not follow the camera. The camera first spins about its azimuth and then animates to the other side — the final frame shows a different set of side faces than the initial view, proving the camera really moved instead of a 2D-flattened face.

math-calculus-sequence-limit.title: Sequence limit: a_n = 1 + 1/n approaching 1
math-calculus-sequence-limit.expect: A row of points crowds denser as n grows and settles onto the dashed line y=1 without ever crossing it.

math-calculus-squeeze-theorem.title: Squeeze theorem: x·sin(1/x) squeezed by ±x
math-calculus-squeeze-theorem.expect: The high-frequency oscillating curve in the middle stays between the two lines y=x and y=-x, and both ends collapse to the origin together.

math-calculus-taylor-sin.title: Taylor expansion: polynomials approaching sin x order by order
math-calculus-taylor-sin.expect: The degree-1, 3, 5 and 7 polynomials each hug the sine curve more closely, matching first near the origin and diverging farther away; the formula on the right grows term by term into the full polynomial (degrees 1 through 7, no term missing) and finally takes the colour of the degree-7 curve.

math-calculus-e-definition.title: Definition of e: (1+1/n)^n increases monotonically towards e
math-calculus-e-definition.expect: The point sequence rises monotonically as n grows and always stays below the dashed line y=e.

math-calculus-mean-value-theorem.title: Lagrange mean value theorem: secant parallel to tangent
math-calculus-mean-value-theorem.expect: The chord through the endpoints (blue secant) is parallel to the tangent (yellow) at some interior point, and the tangency point lands exactly at the midpoint x=1.

math-calculus-upper-lower-sum.title: Upper and lower integrals: two sampling rules bracketing the true value
math-calculus-upper-lower-sum.expect: Left-endpoint (low) and right-endpoint (high) rectangle sets drawn on the same partition: the solid yellow blocks stay inside the curve while the top edges of the blue stroked frames stay above it; each set carries its label (upper sum / lower sum) so the comparison is immediate.

math-calculus-accumulation-function.title: Accumulation function: the area function S(x) and its derivative
math-calculus-accumulation-function.expect: The area under the curve grows block by block to the right while the number S(x) on the right grows with it; at the end the page states S'(x)=f(x).

math-calculus-partial-derivative.title: Partial derivatives: slopes seen with y fixed and with x fixed
math-calculus-partial-derivative.expect: The left panel draws how f changes with x at y=1 fixed, the right how f changes with y at x=1 fixed; each panel carries a yellow tangent through the point (1, 1.2), with slopes 0.8 and 1.6 — the right one visibly steeper.

math-calculus-gradient-descent.title: Gradient descent: stepping along the negative gradient towards the minimum
math-calculus-gradient-descent.expect: Five concentric ellipses are the contour lines (lower towards the centre); the polyline zigzags from the outer ring towards the centre — steps alternate on both sides of the valley along the negative gradient and shrink; arrows mark each step's direction.

math-calculus-double-integral-grid.title: Double integral: cutting the region into small squares
math-calculus-double-integral-grid.expect: The rectangular region is tiled with small cells; cells inside the circle are highlighted and boundary cells count only partly.

math-calculus-fourier-square.title: Fourier series approaching a square wave
math-calculus-fourier-square.expect: A square wave (step-shaped) overlaid with four partial-sum curves: more terms make the flat parts flatter and the jumps steeper, yet a small overshoot always remains near each jump (the Gibbs phenomenon).

math-calculus-series-partial-sums.title: Partial sums: harmonic series diverges vs Σ1/n² converges
math-calculus-series-partial-sums.expect: The blue line (harmonic partial sums) climbs without levelling off; the yellow line (1/n² partial sums) flattens quickly and stops.

math-linear-matrix-vector-product.title: Matrix times vector = linear combination of columns
math-linear-matrix-vector-product.expect: The two column vectors a₁ / a₂ (blue, green) are scaled by their coefficients and assembled into a parallelogram; the diagonal is A·x.

math-linear-determinant-area.title: Geometric meaning of the determinant: the unit square's area scales by |det|
math-linear-determinant-area.expect: The yellow unit square in the grid is stretched into a parallelogram; its area goes from 1 to 2 (det=2).

math-linear-singular-matrix.title: Singular matrix: det=0 collapses the whole plane onto a line
math-linear-singular-matrix.expect: The grid and the yellow square collapse onto one slanted line; the square can never regain an area.

math-linear-orthogonal-projection.title: Orthogonal projection: the shadow of b on a
math-linear-orthogonal-projection.expect: A dashed line drops perpendicularly from the tip of b onto the line a, with a right-angle mark at the intersection; the yellow arrow is the projection vector.

math-linear-gram-schmidt.title: Gram–Schmidt: subtracting the projection onto the first vector
math-linear-gram-schmidt.expect: The green vector slides along the dashed line to the red position and then stands at a right angle to the blue vector (right-angle mark at the intersection).

math-linear-eigen-decomposition.title: Eigen directions: vectors whose direction survives the map
math-linear-eigen-decomposition.expect: On the two dashed directions the vectors stay on the same line after the map (only stretched or shortened) while a third vector visibly deflects. The three pre-image vectors stay in the frame as translucent ghosts, forming a before/after comparison with the solid post-image vectors.

math-linear-rank-nullspace.title: Null space: the directions mapped to 0
math-linear-rank-nullspace.expect: The arrow along (-2,1) (red) collapses to a point after the map (a red dot at the origin); the other direction (green) maps to twice its length.

math-linear-basis-change.title: Basis change: two coordinate systems for the same vector
math-linear-basis-change.expect: The blue basis and the green basis close into a parallelogram (the 0.6·b₂ closing edge drawn as a green dashed line, labelled 1.2·b₁ / 0.6·b₂); the way the yellow vector travels along them is (1.2, 0.6). Read against the standard basis, the same arrow has a different pair of coordinates.

math-linear-rotation-composition.title: Composing rotation matrices: two 30° turns equal one 60° turn
math-linear-rotation-composition.expect: Grid and yellow square are turned 30° and then 30° again; the final pose coincides exactly with the single 60° turn (dashed reference).

math-linear-least-squares.title: Least squares: fitted line and residuals
math-linear-least-squares.expect: A blue fitted line above five data points, with each point's vertical residual drawn as a grey dashed line of obvious length.

math-linear-quadratic-form.title: Quadratic forms: positive-definite ellipses vs indefinite hyperbolas
math-linear-quadratic-form.expect: Concentric ellipses on the left (positive definite: every direction curves upward), a pair of hyperbola branches on the right (indefinite: some direction curves downward).

math-linear-svd-geometry.title: Geometric meaning of SVD: rotate, stretch, rotate again
math-linear-svd-geometry.expect: The yellow circle becomes a tilted ellipse in three steps (rotate 40°, stretch along the axes, rotate -25°); the middle step shows plainly that the two directions are stretched differently.

math-prob-inclusion-exclusion.title: Addition rule (inclusion–exclusion): P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A∩B)
math-prob-inclusion-exclusion.expect: Inside the sample space Ω two translucent rectangular events A and B overlap, the overlap mixing into an intermediate colour; A∩B is lit separately with a red stroked frame and a letter label, then the formula shows it is exactly the part counted twice.

math-prob-conditional-probability.title: Conditional probability: renormalizing on a new sample space
math-prob-conditional-probability.expect: Event A is cut in two by B's boundary; the half inside B is lit first, then everything outside B dims as a whole and only the interior of B is rescaled proportionally.

math-prob-bayes-tree.title: Bayes' formula: a tree combining prior and likelihood into posterior
math-prob-bayes-tree.expect: A two-level branching tree on the left lays out the two routes sick 1% × detected 99% and healthy 99% × false alarm 5%; the right lists both joint probabilities — the green total positive probability is the denominator and the red route's share is the posterior.

math-prob-expectation-balance.title: Expectation: the centre of mass of a distribution, and this lever's fulcrum
math-prob-expectation-balance.expect: Blocks whose heights are proportional to probabilities stand at six values, and the lever balances exactly at the weighted mean μ=3.6 — not at the arithmetic centre 3.5.

math-prob-variance-spread.title: Variance measures spread: same expectation, different scatter
math-prob-variance-spread.expect: Two data sets share one number line and one mean tick, yet one crowds into a clump while the other spreads wide; two range bars with end ticks mark each spread, and the visual gap corresponds directly to variances 2 and 200.

math-prob-law-of-large-numbers.title: Law of large numbers: frequency settling onto the true probability
math-prob-law-of-large-numbers.expect: A polyline starts with violent oscillation and narrows towards the dashed line y=0.5 as trials accumulate — convergence holds with probability 1, not monotonically at every step.

math-prob-central-limit-theorem.title: Central limit theorem: sums of i.i.d. variables approach the normal shape
math-prob-central-limit-theorem.expect: Three histograms side by side: one die (flat), the sum of two (triangular), the sum of four (clearly bell-shaped); the right two pile towards the middle with collapsing tails, normalized to equal height so the shapes compare.

math-prob-poisson-arrivals.title: Poisson distribution: rare-event arrivals on a time axis
math-prob-poisson-arrivals.expect: Arrival times scattered unevenly along a time axis (events cannot overlap), beside the count distribution bars: highest around k=2, 3 and decaying fast at both ends.

math-prob-normal-sigma.title: The 3σ rule of the normal distribution: how the area under the bell splits
math-prob-normal-sigma.expect: Dashed cuts at ±1σ, ±2σ and ±3σ under the bell with the covered areas listed on the right; below, 1000 sample dots crowd the middle and the few beyond ±2.5σ are coloured red.

math-prob-monte-carlo-pi.title: Monte Carlo estimate of π: scatter points and count those inside the quarter circle
math-prob-monte-carlo-pi.expect: A quarter circle inside a square of side 2 with blue points scattered at random: those inside the arc turn yellow, the rest stay blue; the bottom-right readout shows the running ratio times 4 approaching 3.14.

math-prob-random-walk.title: Random walk: memoryless steps, yet a √n scale overall
math-prob-random-walk.expect: Four independent one-dimensional walks leave the origin together, each wandering out of sync; the endpoints are marked and the horizontal envelope around them is far narrower than the step count — the typical scale is √n, not n.

math-prob-hypothesis-test.title: The two errors of hypothesis testing: α rejects the true, β accepts the false
math-prob-hypothesis-test.expect: Two offset bell curves stand for H0 and H1; H0's right tail is cut into a red region (type I / false positive) and H1's left tail into a yellow region (type II / false negative), with the vertical line between them as the rejection threshold.

math-group-cyclic-rotation-group.title: Cyclic group C4: four rotations of a square return to the start
math-group-cyclic-rotation-group.expect: Four squares in a row with a red dot marking the tracked corner: each 90° counter-clockwise turn moves the dot to the next corner; R90 twice lands exactly on R180 and one more turn after R270 returns to R0.

math-group-cayley-table.title: Cayley table: one table from which the three group axioms read off
math-group-cayley-table.expect: The 4×4 addition table of (Z/4, +) filled in: the first row (the identity e=0 row) matches the header exactly, and the paired 1↔3, 2↔2 near the main diagonal are mutual inverses — no empty cell, so the operation is closed.

math-group-dihedral-symmetry.title: Dihedral group D4: the 8 symmetries of a square (4 rotations + 4 reflections)
math-group-dihedral-symmetry.expect: The top row shows rotations by 0° / 90° / 180° / 270°, the bottom row the reflections across the vertical axis, the horizontal axis and the two diagonals; the marked point lands on 8 distinct positions, proving the 8 transformations are pairwise different.

math-group-modular-multiplication.title: Multiplicative group (Z/7)*: generators and orders at a glance
math-group-modular-multiplication.expect: Two circles carry the same six elements 1–6. The left connects arrows by multiply by 2 mod 7 and walks out two disconnected small cycles; the right connects by multiply by 3 mod 7 and one line threads all six elements back to the start.

math-group-generator-subgroups.title: Subgroups generated by a generator: the order always divides the group order
math-group-generator-subgroups.expect: The top row of 12 dots is all of (Z/12, +); the four rows below light up the dots reachable by ⟨1⟩ ⟨2⟩ ⟨3⟩ ⟨4⟩ — 12, 6, 4 and 3 dots in turn, the rest staying dim.

math-group-lagrange-theorem.title: Lagrange's theorem: cosets partition the group, blocks × block size = group size
math-group-lagrange-theorem.expect: Twelve elements in a row coloured green / yellow / blue by coset — exactly 4 per colour, 12 across three colours with no overlap; the colours alternate along the row (0 green 1 yellow 2 blue 3 green…), showing cosets interleave without ever sharing an element.

math-group-permutation-composition.title: Composing permutations: order matters
math-group-permutation-composition.expect: Four rows of three ball positions: the top two rows work out σ then τ step by step, the bottom row swaps to τ then σ; the two final colour orders differ visibly — same set, same operation, different order, different answer.

math-group-homomorphism-kernel.title: Homomorphisms: the bigger the kernel, the smaller the image
math-group-homomorphism-kernel.expect: Each of the six elements of Z/6 on the left draws an arrow to its image in Z/3 on the right; the two red arrows from 0 and 3 hit the same point 0 — those two elements form the kernel, exactly 2; all three points on the right are covered, so the image has 3 elements.

math-group-quotient-group.title: Quotient group G/N: gluing each coset into one new element
math-group-quotient-group.expect: On the left, Z/6 splits into three columns, each a coset; each column contracts into one thick dot below, giving a G/N of only 3 elements. The new addition table on the right shows these 3 elements form a group themselves, with the structure of Z/3.

math-group-subgroup-lattice.title: Subgroup lattice: all subgroups of Z/12 as a poset diagram
math-group-subgroup-lattice.expect: Six nodes ordered by inclusion — all of Z/12 at the top, {0} at the bottom, orders 6, 4, 3, 2 in between; edges appear only between directly-including nodes, forming a lattice.

math-group-symmetric-group-order.title: The order of the symmetric group explodes as n!
math-group-symmetric-group-order.expect: The six bar heights scale only by log10(n!), so the picture looks like a gentle rise; but the true values printed on top jump from 2 all the way to 5040 — growth wildly out of proportion.

math-group-orbit-stabilizer.title: Orbit and stabilizer: where a point goes, and what keeps it fixed
math-group-orbit-stabilizer.expect: On the left square, vertex 1 is pushed by the group action to positions 2, 3, 4 (three green arrows, vertex in yellow) — an orbit of 4 points; the two small squares at the bottom right draw the two symmetries that keep vertex 1 fixed (identity, reflection across the diagonal). Orbit size times stabilizer size equals the group order.

math-discrete-truth-table.title: Truth table: p → q and ¬p ∨ q equivalent row by row
math-discrete-truth-table.expect: A five-column table with all values of p, q, ¬p, p→q and ¬p∨q filled in; the last two columns are circled together in green — identical cell by cell across all four rows, labelled equivalent on the right.

math-discrete-power-set-lattice.title: Power-set lattice: the 8 subsets of {1,2,3} as a cube
math-discrete-power-set-lattice.expect: Eight nodes in four layers by subset size: ∅ on top, three each in the two middle layers, {1,2,3} at the bottom; edges only between nodes differing by one element. The whole shape is a planar projection of a 3-cube.

math-discrete-relation-matrix.title: Relation matrix: reading reflexivity and symmetry off a matrix
math-discrete-relation-matrix.expect: A 4×4 grid of ordered pairs on {1,2,3,4}, filled cells meaning the relation holds. A green box circles the main diagonal (reflexive) and a yellow box a pair mirrored across it (symmetric) — the pattern is unchanged when flipped.

math-discrete-equivalence-classes.title: Equivalence classes: congruence mod 3 cuts 0–8 into three piles
math-discrete-equivalence-classes.expect: The nine digits 0–8 in a line on top; below they are rearranged into three rows of three — each congruent triple grouped and circled in green, the three groups disjoint and together covering all nine digits.

math-discrete-hasse-diagram.title: Hasse diagram: only cover relations; incomparable elements at a glance
math-discrete-hasse-diagram.expect: {1,2,3,6} ordered by divisibility into a diamond — 1 at the bottom, 6 at the top, 2 and 3 side by side in the middle; no edge between 2 and 3, labelled incomparable. The transitive relation from 1 to 6 is also left undrawn.

math-discrete-mathematical-induction.title: The classic picture of induction: two staircases making one rectangle
math-discrete-mathematical-induction.expect: The blue staircase on the left has column heights 1, 2, 3, 4 and the yellow one on the right 4, 3, 2, 1; interleaved they exactly fill a rectangle 4 wide and 5 high — so the staircase's total cell count is half of 4×5.

math-discrete-pigeonhole.title: Pigeonhole principle: 13 pigeons into 12 holes
math-discrete-pigeonhole.expect: Twelve holes each take one pigeon first, leaving one with nowhere to go; when it lands in the first hole a red circle marks it — the holes are used up, so some hole must hold two.

math-discrete-bipartite-graph.title: Bipartite graphs: vertices split in two, edges only across
math-discrete-bipartite-graph.expect: Six vertices in a blue and a yellow column on the left with all six edges crossing from blue to yellow and none inside a column; a triangle on the right as the counterexample — an odd cycle of three edges head to tail.

math-discrete-graph-coloring.title: Graph colouring: adjacent vertices differ; how few colours suffice
math-discrete-graph-coloring.expect: On the left a 5-cycle where red and blue alone collide at the closure, forcing a third colour (green); on the right four mutually adjacent vertices that need all four colours however arranged.

math-discrete-spanning-tree.title: Minimum spanning tree: add edges by weight, drop those that close a cycle
math-discrete-spanning-tree.expect: All 8 weighted edges first laid faintly over six vertices, then judged in weight order 1→8 — adopted edges light up green (5 of them, exactly connecting the 6 points into a tree), cycle-forming edges turn red and dashed. The 5 green edges total weight 19.

math-discrete-euler-hamilton.title: Euler vs Hamilton cycles: one counts edges, the other counts vertices
math-discrete-euler-hamilton.expect: On the left two triangles sharing a vertex: the centre vertex has degree 4 and the rest 2, all even, so every edge can be traversed exactly once in one stroke (Euler cycle), but visiting every vertex exactly once is impossible. On the right a quadrilateral with one diagonal: the outer ring visits all four vertices (Hamilton cycle), but two vertices have degree 3, so no Euler cycle exists.

math-discrete-hanoi-recurrence.title: The Hanoi recurrence: T(n) = 2T(n−1) + 1, hence 2ⁿ − 1
math-discrete-hanoi-recurrence.expect: Three pegs at the bottom left with three discs stacked small-to-large on the first; the bar chart on the right gives the move counts for n=1 to 8. Bar heights scale by log₂(T+1), so the picture rises in perfectly even steps — a straight line standing for genuine exponential growth.

syntax-comprehensions.title: Syntax: comprehensions, unpacking and generator expressions building a scene
syntax-comprehensions.expect: The mobjects built by comprehensions, unpacking and generator expressions match the source logic in count and layout (the print assertions are authoritative).

syntax-closures-itertools.title: Syntax: closures, generator functions and itertools chains
syntax-closures-itertools.expect: Closures, generator functions and itertools chains build their mobjects normally, with counts matching the itertools output.

syntax-dataclass-decorator.title: Syntax: dataclass, decorators and class attributes together
syntax-dataclass-decorator.expect: dataclass, decorators and class attributes run through; the mobjects built match the data.

syntax-try-context.title: Syntax: exception handling, context managers and custom exceptions
syntax-try-context.expect: The exception is caught and the context manager enters and exits normally (the print assertions are authoritative); the picture renders normally.

syntax-unpack-format.title: Syntax: unpacking, formatting, slicing and sorting
syntax-unpack-format.expect: Unpacking, formatting and slice/sort results are correct (the print assertions are authoritative).

syntax-group-iteration.title: Syntax: iterating a VGroup (for, comprehension, out-of-range index)
syntax-group-iteration.expect: for over a VGroup terminates normally (it does not iterate forever) and an out-of-range index raises IndexError.

api-colors.title: API roll call: the colour constants (all 76 usable colours)
api-colors.expect: 76 squares in rows of 10 forming a palette, each filled with its own name (red, yellow, blue, green, purple, grey, brown… all distinct) — not a field of black (black was the set_stroke-wipes-fill incident, now fixed).

api-rates.title: API roll call: all 16 rate functions
api-rates.expect: Sixteen rows, each a rate name plus one dot: every dot travels left to right over the same distance, but each row's pacing is its name — smooth starts fast and eases out, rush_into bolts from the start, there_and_back turns back at the end, wiggle jitters in place. What is observed is not the endpoint but how it gets there.

api-const.title: API roll call: direction and axis constants
api-const.expect: Several arrows pointing in the directions the RIGHT / UP / OUT constants name, directions matching the names; placements involving axis constants are not skewed.

api-methods.title: API roll call: the method surface (rewrites, geometry reads, coordinate mapping)
api-methods.expect: The method surface exercised item by item: style rewrites, geometry reads and coordinate mapping all pass their print assertions, and the marked points and lines land where expected on screen.

api-classes-2d.title: API roll call: shapes and markers (ok in the table, unused by the corpus)
api-classes-2d.expect: A grid layout: each named shape occupies one cell with its name label under the cell, nothing overlapping and everything inside the canvas.

api-classes-3d.title: API roll call: matrices, tables, 3D and miscellany
api-classes-3d.expect: A grid layout: one 3D solid per cell (each coloured and shaded with volume, not a black block), four matrices per row, four miscellany per row, name labels beside the cells, nothing overlapping and everything inside the canvas.

api-scenes.title: API roll call: the scene family
